subject: Clarify: netting/sweep vs single transfer for EUR invoice + intermediary fees
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <ap@cardiometrics.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14 07:12 +01:00
Subject: Payment method question for Invoice #1234 - sweep vs single wire

Hi Marissa,

We received Invoice #1234 for June SaaS usage (EUR 48,250) and our treasury team is asking whether Redwood prefers a single SWIFT transfer for the full amount or our nightly collection sweep (we operate a multibank sweep that consolidates payments, which may route via an intermediary bank).

A couple of specific questions from treasury:
- If we use the sweep, will intermediary/correspondent bank fees likely be deducted en route?
- Does Redwood require amounts to arrive "gross" (i.e., CardioMetrics covers intermediary fees) or is it acceptable for fees to be deducted (net of fees)?
- Any special fields we should populate on the payment instruction (eg. specific SWIFT field for instruction to beneficiary/OUR vs BEN vs SHA)?
- We also need to confirm VAT handling: should we include VAT on the wire remittance or will Redwood issue a reverse-charge style invoice?

Attached: our PO and the planned wire template from our bank.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Claire Dawson
Head of AP, CardioMetrics
accounts-payable@cardiometrics.co
+44 20 7946 0xxx

Attachment: cardiometrics_wire_template.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <ap@cardiometrics.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14 10:04 +02:00
Subject: Re: Payment method question for Invoice #1234 - sweep vs single wire

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear questions. Summary up front: we prefer the beneficiary to receive the full invoiced amount (gross) and recommend using a single wire if possible to avoid multiple intermediary legs and unpredictable deductions. If you must use a sweep that routes through a correspondent bank, please ask your bank to send fees as 'SHA' (split) and include the invoice number in the remittance so any deductions can be reconciled.

Details / options:
1) Preferred (single SWIFT / OUR) — ask your bank to send as OUR so CardioMetrics covers any correspondent fees. This guarantees Redwood receives the full EUR 48,250. If your bank cannot send OUR, 'SHA' is acceptable but note that intermediary banks may deduct a small amount en route.

2) Sweep / multi-leg collection — acceptable, but:
   - Provide the exact remittance text: "Invoice 1234 / CardioMetrics Inc. / PO 2028-06-CM"
   - If intermediary fees are deducted, we will need a bank stub showing amounts + BICs to reconcile. Please request your bank to provide a beneficiary bank-stub pdf when the transaction posts.

3) Bank fields — include the following in the instruction to reduce ambiguity:
   - Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Inc.
   - IBAN: GB33BUKB20201234567890 (EUR settlement account)
   - BIC/SWIFT: BUKBGB22
   - For intermediary/correspondent bank info (if your bank requests it): Correspondent: DEUTDEFFXXX, Account: 100234567890 (ASK your bank to fill correspondent details; do not alter the beneficiary IBAN)

4) Net vs Gross / VAT: Redwood is a US-headquartered vendor. For EU B2B customers with a valid VAT ID we can issue a reverse-charge invoice (no VAT on the invoice). Please send your VAT registration number and we will re-issue the invoice as reverse-charge. If CardioMetrics is paying from an entity without a VAT ID, we will include VAT on the invoice.

Attachments: I'm attaching an internal Redwood bank-stub template you can pass to your treasury team and an updated invoice that will include the VAT line if you confirm you need it.

Next steps:
- If you can confirm whether your bank can send OUR vs SHA, we'll confirm the final invoice PDF (reverse-charge or standard).
- If you proceed with sweep, please forward the bank stub once sent so we can reconcile quickly.

Happy to take a 15-min call if your treasury prefers — propose 14:00 BST today.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0199

Attachments: redwood-bank-stub.png (image), 2028-06-Invoice-CardioMetrics-1234.pdf (pdf)

Best,

Claire — thanks for the quick confirmation and the VAT ID. We have re-issued the invoice as reverse-charge and attached the v2 PDF (2028-06-Invoice-CardioMetrics-1234-v2.pdf). Please confirm when the OUR wire posts and share the bank stub.

A few bookkeeping notes for your AP team to avoid delays:
- Please include the invoice number exactly as "Invoice 1234" in the payment reference. That lets our automated reconciliation apply the payment without manual intervention.
- Even with OUR ordering, some intermediary banks will still show a trace; please provide the bank confirmation (MT103 or bank stub) if any amount is missing on our side.
- If you expect recurring sweeps and would like a standing arrangement (e.g., we accept net-of-fees with a small monthly tolerance), let me know and I can route to Finance (Laura) to set a policy and update the invoice workflow.

If the wire posts today we’ll mark the invoice as paid on receipt of the stub and reply with a payment receipt.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Regards,
Marissa
